after.name: Question 1
after.problem:
Given the vector $x$ and the system of linear equations below, find the projection of $x$ onto the solution space of the system.

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 5\end{aligned}],\,{\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}-4{x}_{3}=0 \\ 6{x}_{1}-12{x}_{3}=0\end{aligned}
$$
after.worked_solution:
First, we need to find a basis for the solution space of the system. 

Consider the augmented matrix $M$ of the system, which we reduce to row echelon form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & -4 & 0 \\ 6 & 0 & -12 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & -4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is $1$ pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2},\,{x}_{3}$ are free variables. Now, from the first equation, we get ${x}_{1}=2{x}_{3}.$ Therefore, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}2{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]={x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{3}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2},\,{x}_{3}\in R.
$$

Consequently, $B={[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}$ is the basis of the solution space of the system.

Now, we find the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the solution space of the system:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & =A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T}\,x \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot {([\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 0 \\ 2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}])}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 0 \\ 2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot {[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 5\end{aligned}]}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ 5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}5 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ 5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Orthogonal Projection of a Vector Onto the Solution Space of a Linear System
content.problem:
Given the vector $x$ and the system of linear equations below, find the projection of $x$ onto the solution space of the system.

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 5\end{aligned}],\,{\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}-4{x}_{3}=0 \\ 6{x}_{1}-12{x}_{3}=0\end{aligned}
$$
content.worked_solution:
First, we need to find a basis for the solution space of the system. 

Consider the augmented matrix $M$ of the system, which we reduce to row echelon form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & -4 & 0 \\ 6 & 0 & -12 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & -4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is $1$ pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2},\,{x}_{3}$ are free variables. Now, from the first equation, we get ${x}_{1}=2{x}_{3}.$ Therefore, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}2{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]={x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{3}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2},\,{x}_{3}\in R.
$$

Consequently, $B={[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}$ is the basis of the solution space of the system.

Now, we find the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the solution space of the system:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & =A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T}\,x \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot {([\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 0 \\ 2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}])}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 0 \\ 2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot {[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 5\end{aligned}]}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ 5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}5 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ 5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 2
after.problem:
Given the vector $x$ and the system of linear equations below, find the projection of $x$ onto the solution space of the system.

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}-20 \\ 5 \\ -8\end{aligned}],\,{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}-3{x}_{3}=0 \\ 4{x}_{1}+12{x}_{2}-12{x}_{3}=0\end{aligned}
$$
after.worked_solution:
First, we need to find a basis for the solution space of the system. 

Consider the augmented matrix $M$ of the system, which we reduce to row echelon form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & -3 & 0 \\ 4 & 12 & -12 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-4{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & -3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is $1$ pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2},\,{x}_{3}$ are free variables. Now, from the first equation, we get ${x}_{1}=-3{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3}.$ Therefore, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}-3{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]={x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{3}[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2},\,{x}_{3}\in R.
$$

Consequently, $B={[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}$ is the basis of the solution space of the system.

Now, we find the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the solution space of the system:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & =A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T}\,x \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & 3 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot {([\begin{aligned}-3 & 1 & 0 \\ 3 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}-3 & 3 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}])}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}-3 & 1 & 0 \\ 3 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}-20 \\ 5 \\ -8\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & 3 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot {[\begin{aligned}10 & -9 \\ -9 & 10\end{aligned}]}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}65 \\ -68\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & 3 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{19}[\begin{aligned}10 & 9 \\ 9 & 10\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}65 \\ -68\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & 3 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 \\ -5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-21 \\ 2 \\ -5\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Orthogonal Projection of a Vector Onto the Solution Space of a Linear System
content.problem:
Given the vector $x$ and the system of linear equations below, find the projection of $x$ onto the solution space of the system.

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}-20 \\ 5 \\ -8\end{aligned}],\,{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}-3{x}_{3}=0 \\ 4{x}_{1}+12{x}_{2}-12{x}_{3}=0\end{aligned}
$$
content.worked_solution:
First, we need to find a basis for the solution space of the system. 

Consider the augmented matrix $M$ of the system, which we reduce to row echelon form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & -3 & 0 \\ 4 & 12 & -12 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-4{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & -3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is $1$ pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2},\,{x}_{3}$ are free variables. Now, from the first equation, we get ${x}_{1}=-3{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3}.$ Therefore, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}-3{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]={x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{3}[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2},\,{x}_{3}\in R.
$$

Consequently, $B={[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}$ is the basis of the solution space of the system.

Now, we find the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the solution space of the system:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & =A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T}\,x \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & 3 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot {([\begin{aligned}-3 & 1 & 0 \\ 3 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}-3 & 3 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}])}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}-3 & 1 & 0 \\ 3 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}-20 \\ 5 \\ -8\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & 3 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot {[\begin{aligned}10 & -9 \\ -9 & 10\end{aligned}]}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}65 \\ -68\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & 3 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{19}[\begin{aligned}10 & 9 \\ 9 & 10\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}65 \\ -68\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & 3 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 \\ -5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-21 \\ 2 \\ -5\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 3
after.problem:
Given the vector $x$ and the system of linear equations below, find the projection of $x$ onto the solution space of the system.

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}-8 \\ 1 \\ -8\end{aligned}],\,{\begin{aligned}3{x}_{1}-6{x}_{2}-9{x}_{3}=0 \\ -2{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2}+6{x}_{3}=0\end{aligned}
$$
after.worked_solution:
First, we need to find a basis for the solution space of the system. 

Consider the augmented matrix $M$ of the system, which we reduce to row echelon form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -6 & -9 & 0 \\ -2 & 4 & 6 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -3 & 0 \\ -2 & 4 & 6 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

 

In the reduced matrix above, there is $1$ pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2},\,{x}_{3}$ are free variables. Now, from the first equation, we get ${x}_{1}=2{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3}.$ Therefore, the general solution is 

$$
[\begin{aligned}2{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]={x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{3}[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2},\,{x}_{3}\in R.
$$

Consequently, $B={[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}$ is the basis of the solution space of the system. 

Now, we find the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the solution space of the system:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & =A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T}\,x \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot {([\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & 0 \\ 3 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}])}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & 0 \\ 3 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}-8 \\ 1 \\ -8\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot {[\begin{aligned}5 & 6 \\ 6 & 10\end{aligned}]}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}-15 \\ -32\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{14}[\begin{aligned}10 & -6 \\ -6 & 5\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}-15 \\ -32\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{14}[\begin{aligned}42 \\ -70\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}3 \\ -5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-9 \\ 3 \\ -5\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Orthogonal Projection of a Vector Onto the Solution Space of a Linear System
content.problem:
Given the vector $x$ and the system of linear equations below, find the projection of $x$ onto the solution space of the system.

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}-8 \\ 1 \\ -8\end{aligned}],\,{\begin{aligned}3{x}_{1}-6{x}_{2}-9{x}_{3}=0 \\ -2{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2}+6{x}_{3}=0\end{aligned}
$$
content.worked_solution:
First, we need to find a basis for the solution space of the system. 

Consider the augmented matrix $M$ of the system, which we reduce to row echelon form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -6 & -9 & 0 \\ -2 & 4 & 6 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -3 & 0 \\ -2 & 4 & 6 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

 

In the reduced matrix above, there is $1$ pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2},\,{x}_{3}$ are free variables. Now, from the first equation, we get ${x}_{1}=2{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3}.$ Therefore, the general solution is 

$$
[\begin{aligned}2{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]={x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{3}[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2},\,{x}_{3}\in R.
$$

Consequently, $B={[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}$ is the basis of the solution space of the system. 

Now, we find the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the solution space of the system:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & =A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T}\,x \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot {([\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & 0 \\ 3 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}])}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & 0 \\ 3 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}-8 \\ 1 \\ -8\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot {[\begin{aligned}5 & 6 \\ 6 & 10\end{aligned}]}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}-15 \\ -32\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{14}[\begin{aligned}10 & -6 \\ -6 & 5\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}-15 \\ -32\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{14}[\begin{aligned}42 \\ -70\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}3 \\ -5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-9 \\ 3 \\ -5\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 4
after.problem:
Find the acute angle between the vector $x$ and the subspace spanned by the linearly independent vectors ${{a}_{1},{a}_{2}},$ where

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 3\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].
$$
after.worked_solution:
The orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace spanned by the columns of a matrix $A$ is given by

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x=A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T}\,x.
$$

In our case, we have

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ {a}_{1} & {a}_{2} \\ | & |\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}]\,⟹\,{A}^{T}=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 2 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, we get the following projection:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}]\cdot {([\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 2 & 3\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}])}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 2 & 3\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -1 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}]\cdot {[\begin{aligned}5 & 8 \\ 8 & 14\end{aligned}]}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}3 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{6}[\begin{aligned}14 & -8 \\ -8 & 5\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}3 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}6 \\ -3\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 0 \\ 3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The acute angle between $x$ and $S$ is the acute angle between $x$ and ${\text{proj}}_{S}x.$ Equivalently, it is the acute angle between $x$ and any non-zero vector that is parallel to ${\text{proj}}_{S}x.$ So, to make calculations easier, we can find the angle between the vectors

$\,$ $x=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,2\,{\text{proj}}_{S}x=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 0 \\ 3\end{aligned}].$

Computing the cosine using the dot product, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\frac{(-1)\cdot (-3)+(-1)\cdot 0+2\cdot 3}{\sqrt{(-1)^{2}+(-1)^{2}+{2}^{2}}\sqrt{(-3)^{2}+{0}^{2}+{3}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{9}{\sqrt{6}\sqrt{18}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
\theta =\operatorname{arccos}⁡(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2})=\frac{\pi }{6},
$$

which is already an acute angle.

decision.explanation: A normal to the plane is n=(−1,1,2), perpendicular to both spanning vectors. The angle θ to the plane satisfies sin(θ)=|x·n|/(‖x‖‖n‖)=6/(√54·√6)=1/3. Thus θ=arcsin(1/3)≈19.47°, option d.

after.name: Question 5
after.problem:
Find the acute angle between the vector $x$ and the subspace spanned by the linearly independent vectors ${{a}_{1},{a}_{2}},$ where

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,\,x=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -5 \\ 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Round the answer to $2$ decimal places.
after.worked_solution:
The orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace spanned by the columns of a matrix $A$ is given by

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x=A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T}\,x.
$$

In our case, we have

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ {a}_{1} & {a}_{2} \\ | & |\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 2 & 1 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}]\,⟹\,{A}^{T}=[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

 

Therefore, we get the following projection: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 2 & 1 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}]\cdot {([\begin{aligned}2 & 2 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 2 & 1 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}])}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 & 2 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}5 \\ -5 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 2 & 1 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}]\cdot {[\begin{aligned}8 & 0 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}]}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 \\ -12\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 2 & 1 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{8} & 0 \\ 0 & \frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 \\ -12\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 2 & 1 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 \\ -4\end{aligned}] \\  & =4[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

 

The acute angle between $x$ and $S$ is the acute angle between $x$ and ${\text{proj}}_{S}x.$ Equivalently, it is the acute angle between $x$ and any non-zero vector that is parallel to ${\text{proj}}_{S}x.$ So, to make calculations easier, we can find the angle between the vectors

$\,$ $x=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -5 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,\frac{1}{4}\,{\text{proj}}_{S}x=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

Computing the cosine using the dot product, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\frac{x\cdot {\text{proj}}_{S}x}{‖x‖‖{\text{proj}}_{S}x‖} \\  & =\frac{5\cdot 1+(-5)\cdot (-1)+2\cdot 1}{\sqrt{{5}^{2}+(-5)^{2}+{2}^{2}}\cdot \sqrt{{1}^{2}+(-1)^{2}+{1}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{12}{\sqrt{54}\sqrt{3}} \\  & =\frac{12}{9\sqrt{2}} \\  & =\frac{4}{3\sqrt{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, 

$$
\theta =\operatorname{arccos}⁡(\frac{4}{3\sqrt{2}})≈{19.47}^{∘},
$$

which is already an acute angle.
